articles.title: Haven’t received any proposal to join NDA: Supriya Sule
articles.summary: Supriya Sule rules out merger of NCP factions, says talks ended after Ajit Pawar’s death; denies NDA join talks; comments on delimitation proposal.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Even as deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar called on chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday amid continuing speculation about the merger of the two NCP parties, working president of the NCP SP Supriya Sule categorically ruled out the possibility.She reiterated that this issue had reached a full stop the day her cousin, former deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar, was killed in an air crash this Jan.“I am saying this for the final time. When my brother was alive, there were talks on a merger and a date had been fixed. The day he passed away -- in my mind and within our party -- there was a full-stop to this,” she said.She clarified that she had not received any proposal regarding the merger from the NCP. “I have not received any proposal by phone, WhatsApp, letter or any other means of communication,” she said.Responding to media questions on whether the NCP (SP) is considering joining the NDA alliance, she said, “There are no such talks. A full-stop can be spoken of only if talks are on.”Regarding her meetings with NCP leader Praful Patel in recent days, she said the two families have known each other for decades and that both of them were part of several parliamentary committees. “We meet regularly in the parliamentary committee on finance and FCRA. He was among the invitees for my daughter’s wedding,” said Sule.When asked about her response to Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Sanjay Raut’s comment that talk of the merger was a myth and would fade in the next two days, she said, “He is like an elder brother to me and a senior leader in the MVA alliance. He has the right to say what he wants.”On the NCP (SP)’s possible support for the Centre’s delimitation bill, Sule said, “Six months ago, they had discussed this with several leaders of the INDIA bloc including me and Shiv Sena (UBT)’s Arvind Sawant. We felt that if the seats in all parliamentary constituencies uniformly rise by 50%, then there is no harm discussing this. The size of the electorate in each parliamentary constituency has risen from 13-14 lakh to 25-30 lakh and it is difficult for MPs to reach out to the entire constituency,” she saidHowever, she added, “There is no proposal before us at the moment. Nor have we seen the bill.”You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: Swiss men take to streets, call for stronger fight against violence against women
articles.summary: Hundreds of men gathered outside parliament in the Swiss capital on Saturday to protest against misogyny and violence against women, calling on men to
articles.body: Hundreds of men gathered outside parliament in the Swiss capital on Saturday to protest against misogyny and violence against women, calling on men to take a more active and vocal role in challenging both.The demonstration, titled “Men against Violence against Women”, came amid growing concerns over the spread of misogynistic views among teenage boys and young men, particularly online. Organisers and campaigners have called for men to build a stronger counter-narrative to such attitudes.The rally also followed increased visibility for influencers associated with the right-wing “manosphere”, some of whom were emboldened by US President Donald Trump's 2024 election victory to amplify misogynistic insults and threats online, according to news agency the Associated Press (AP).Study highlights concerns over attitudes towards masculinitySwiss academics and advocacy groups have, for the first time, attempted to assess the scale of the manosphere movement in the country.A survey published in June by the University of Zurich and mencare, an umbrella organisation representing Swiss men's and fathers' groups, found that half of male respondents aged 18 to 24 expressed concern that “real men are increasingly marginalized in society”.The study also found that half of those surveyed held a restrictive, dominance-based view of masculinity.It called for “a systematic and society-wide debate about ideals of masculinity that promote violence”, adding that the discussion should begin in schools.The Swiss government has also taken up the issue. Justice Minister Beat Jans attended a conference earlier this month aimed at raising awareness about the dangers of violent online abuse directed at women.In a speech on November 2, Jans cited figures showing that men committed four-fifths of violent crimes. The proportion was even higher in rape cases, where men accounted for 99% of perpetrators, he said.“It is not all men. But we must also admit: It is almost always men,” Jans said. “Violence by men does not begin with the first blow; it begins with a disparaging remark. We men all have a duty.”Organisers call on men to challenge misogynyThe demonstration sought to encourage young men influenced by the manosphere, as well as those exposed to patriarchal attitudes more broadly, to reconsider their views and challenge violence against women and queer people.Christoph Gosteli, a 42-year-old social worker and co-organiser of the rally alongside the group Maenner, said men needed to acknowledge their role in the problem and take responsibility for addressing it.“We men are part of the problem — the problem being violence against women and queer people,” Gosteli said.“That is why it is important for us to take a stand and say: We no longer want to be part of the problem; we want to be part of the solution,” he added.The rally's central message was that men should not remain silent on misogyny and violence, but take a more visible role in opposing them.You use AI every day. articles.title: Tamil Nadu suspends 5 library officials over AI-generated books, fake authors and inflated prices
articles.summary: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has suspended five library officials over the procurement of AI-generated books for the Periyar Arivulagam Library in
articles.body: CHENNAI: The Tamil Nadu government has suspended five library officials over the procurement of AI-generated books for the Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore.According to an announcement made by school education minister A Rajmohan on Sunday, those suspended are S Kamatchi, chief librarian, Anna Centenary Library (ACL), Chennai; Dinesh Kumar, chief librarian and information officer (in-charge), Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai; V Santhanakrishnan, librarian and information officer, Kalaignar Centenary Library, Madurai, and in-charge of the Periyar Arivulagam Library; S Santhana Karthikeyan, librarian and information officer, ACL, Chennai; and J Juliet, chief accounts officer, Directorate of Public Libraries.The minister said the irregularities had occurred during the previous DMK regime.The alleged irregularities came to light after writer Perumal Murugan identified nearly 1,800 books from Agal Vilakku Pathippagam in the library’s fourth-floor Tamil section.The books reportedly carried inflated prices, AI-generated misinformation, fictitious author names and invalid International Standard Book Numbers (ISBNs).Writers and researchers subsequently flagged similar irregularities elsewhere.Researchers have also raised concerns about the library’s English-language books. S Satheesh Kumar, who examined the collection, found more than 200 titles from 3GE Learning Publications with allegedly fake ISBNs.Priced between Rs 6,000 and Rs 9,900, some of the books carried dubious publisher website details and fictitious author credentials.In one instance, a book on electronics and instrumentation listed a Pakistani woman as its editor.When contacted, she said she was an environmental scientist. articles.title: Bay of Bengal cyclone alert: Depression to intensify into severe cyclonic storm by November 17
articles.summary: VISAKHAPATNAM: The well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards and intensified into a depression on Sunday
articles.body: VISAKHAPATNAM: The well-marked low-pressure area over the southeast Bay of Bengal moved north-northwestwards and intensified into a depression on Sunday morning, November 15.The system lay centred over the southeast and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, about 700km west-southwest of Port Blair in the Andaman Islands, 860km east-southeast of Chennai in Tamil Nadu, 1,040km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh and 1,160km south-southeast of Gopalpur in Odisha.According to the weather department, the depression is very likely to continue moving north-northwestwards and intensify further into a cyclonic storm over the central parts of the south and adjoining westcentral Bay of Bengal on Monday, November 16.The system is further expected to intensify into a severe cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal on Tuesday, November 17.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Visakhapatnam | Silver Rate in Visakhapatnam | Bank Holidays in Visakhapatnam | Public Holidays in Visakhapatnam | Petrol Price in Visakhapatnam | Diesel Price in Visakhapatnam | CNG Price in Visakhapatnam | LPG Price in VisakhapatnamStay updated with the latest Visakhapatnam news. articles.title: IndiGo flight’s landing gear fails to retract after take-off, makes safe emergency landing in Pune
articles.summary: PUNE: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight (6E 0623) with 192 persons on board,
articles.body: PUNE: A full emergency was declared at the Pune airport on Sunday morning after a Guwahati bound IndiGo flight (6E 0623) with 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, reported a technical issue shortly after take-off.The pilot informed Air Traffic Control (ATC) that the aircraft’s landing gear (undercarriage) had failed to retract after take-off and remained in the extended position. Airport officials said that immediately upon receiving the information, they coordinated with ATC, IndiGo and all concerned agencies."The Indian Air Force (IAF) declared a Full Emergency, following which all prescribed emergency response procedures were promptly activated. Fire services, ambulance services and other emergency response teams were placed on high alert to ensure the safety of passengers and crew," Pune airport director Santosh Dhoke said.As a precautionary measure, the aircraft conducted a low pass over the runway to facilitate a visual assessment of the landing gear. Subsequently, the aircraft landed safely at Pune Airport at around 9am."Following the landing, the aircraft was escorted to Bay number- 7 by three fire-fighting vehicles and two ambulances, in accordance with the prescribed emergency response procedures. After confirmation of the aircraft’s safe and normal status, ATC declared the full emergency withdrawn at 9.10am. Thereafter, the aerobridge was connected, and all passengers were safely deboarded," the director added.All 192 persons on board, including passengers and crew, were safe, and no injuries were reported. IndiGo is arranging an alternate aircraft from Bengaluru to Pune to facilitate the onward journey of the affected passengers to Guwahati.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘For sure not in 2027’: Nato scraps leaders’ summit in Albania amid defence spending Ukraine war concerns
articles.summary: Nato will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania next year, with the alliance scaling back high-level meetings amid tensions over defence spending, Iran
articles.body: Nato will not hold a leaders' summit in Albania next year, with the alliance scaling back high-level meetings amid tensions over defence spending, Iran and the war in Ukraine.However, Nato secretary-general Mark Rutte played down the decision, saying the alliance was flexible about when to hold such gatherings, AP reported on Monday.On Thursday, Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama said that there was no common position on when the summit would take place, but ruled out 2027. He said Tirana could host the event in 2028 if a summit is held that year.“There is not yet a common position on when the summit will happen, for sure not in 2027,” Rama said. “In 2028, if it will be a summit, it will be in Tirana.”Rutte said the meeting would be held as necessary.“We are flexible with Nato summits,” Rutte told The Associated Press in an interview. “We have summits when we need them,” he said, adding that the next one would be held “when a necessity is there”.Nato previously held summits every two years, until about a decade ago.Ministerial meetings also being scaled backThe reduction in high-level gatherings extends beyond meetings between US President Donald Trump and other Nato leaders.Nato defence ministers usually meet in October, but no meeting was held last month, and none is planned for October 2027. Foreign ministers are scheduled to meet only once next year, instead of twice, under what thealliance describes as a “reorganisation package”.US defence secretary Pete Hegseth and secretary of state Marco Rubio have each skipped a NATO meeting or left before talks concluded since taking office. Hegseth has used defence ministerial gatherings to criticise or pressure European allies and Canada, AP reported.Albania's defence spending raises questionsAlbania was named as the host for next year's summit in 2025, but its name was removed from a declaration issued after a NATO meeting in July.Some allies believe Albania is not spending enough on defence and were reluctant to reward it with the alliance's major event. The government in Tirana is projected to spend 2.15 per cent of its gross domestic product on defence this year.Nato's target is for its 32 members to spend 3.5 per cent of GDP on core defence by 2035, with a further 1.5 per cent allocated to defence-related infrastructure. Albania is not the worst performer among member states, with Spain, Belgium and Slovenia spending considerably less.Hosting a summit carries financial and political costsOrganising a Nato summit requires substantial resources and can carry political costs for the host country.The Netherlands reportedly spent a year preparing for the 2025 summit in The Hague, with an investment of around $100 million. Officials said Nato would have needed to make a decision on Albania by October to give the country enough time to organise next year's event.Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan hosted this year's summit gala at his palace complex in Ankara. According to AP, Turkey refurbished a military airport for the arrival of leaders and deployed tens of thousands of security personnel, effectively shutting down parts of the capital. Non-essential public workers were also given a week off.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Bengaluru man buys liquor worth Rs 2,170, objects to paying Rs 20 for carry bag bearing store's own name and logo; consumer commission calls it unfair trade practice and deficiency in service, orders Tonique to refund Rs 20 and pay Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 3,000 litigation costs
articles.summary: BENGALURU: The bag was meant only to carry the booze home, but it ended up killing the buzz for a liquor store.
articles.body: BENGALURU: The bag was meant only to carry the booze home, but it ended up killing the buzz for a liquor store. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Bangalore (Urban), held a liquor store guilty of unfair trade practice and deficiency in service for charging a Bagalagunte resident Rs 20 for a carry bag stamped with its own name and logo.It all started on June 3, 2025, when Theerthesh BS, 33, bought beverages worth Rs 2,170 from Tonique, a liquor store on Kasturba Road. Since the bottles were fragile, he asked for a carry bag. The store gave him one bearing its brand name, logo and other promotional content, and raised a separate bill of Rs 20 for it on the same day and at the same time.Theerthesh said he objected to paying for a bag that carried the store’s own logo and identification details, but the store’s staff rejected his request. With no other way to carry the bottles safely, he paid. He then filed a complaint on June 17, seeking a refund of Rs 20, compensation of Rs 25,000 for deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, and other relief.Despite notice from the commission, Tonique, represented by its manager, neither appeared nor filed its version, and was placed ex parte. Later, Tonique’s counsel did file written arguments. The store said when a customer asks for a carry bag, they are told about the charges, which are displayed on a board in all its outlets, and a bill is raised. The store thus admitted that it sells carry bags on request after a purchase.The commission, comprising president Ramachandra MS and members Nandini H Kumbhar and Savitha Airani, invoking the principle of “Caveat Venditor”, meaning “let the seller be aware”, said a seller of beverage bottles should know every customer will need a bag to carry such products.Charging customers for a bag used for its own advertising also amounted to deficiency in service and unfair trade practice, it held.The commission further noted that Tonique’s failure to appear was a clear admission of the allegations.
